note: Two sides of porro: the bandas pelayeras of the Sinú (Laguneta, Cereteana, Bajera de San Pelayo, from the Discos Fuentes anthology Historia musical del porro pelayero) and the orchestras that took it to the ballroom from the 1940s to the 1970s (Pedro Laza, Pacho Galán, Lucho Bermúdez, La Sonora Cordobesa, Clímaco Sarmiento, Edmundo Arias, Rufo Garrido), closing with Adriana Lucía's 2010 revival. Borrachera is a Lucho Bermúdez porro played by the Cartagena pianist Ramón Ropaín.

size.basis: A judgement, not a count; no source counts porro recordings. What is on record: the orchestra porros of the 1940s-1970s (Lucho Bermúdez, Pacho Galán, Edmundo Arias, Pedro Laza y sus Pelayeros, La Sonora Cordobesa, Billo's Caracas Boys and others, largely on Discos Fuentes and Sonolux, each with many LPs); the banda pelayera recordings of the Sinú and the savannas (bands of San Pelayo, Laguneta and many towns, festival and local recordings since the Festival Nacional del Porro began in 1977); porros covered by Cuban and Venezuelan bands (Benny Moré, La Sonora Matancera); and later revival and fusion records. The Cartagena paper El Universal published a list of the 100 best porros (2014), which is about the size of the canon; an insider's essential list is about 50 recordings.
